newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended Friday stunted in directionless trade with industrials gasping at lower levels and gold finishing weaker despite bullion's recent recoveries, dealers said.
They said sentiment in the industrials sector had continued to worsen after poor results from some of the market's key industrial companies.
"The whole market is very, very thin. This has been a very disappointing day," Johan Marais, a director at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
"I think the disappointing company results are still the main reason for the weakness in our market," he added.
The Industrial index finished down 19.4 points at 8,421.2, the gold index down 26.8 points at 1,228.3 and the all-share down 30.3 points at 7,142.8.
Among the day's features were financial firm Octodec which added five cents to close at 310 cents following a bookover deal involving about four million shares worth around 12.5 million rand.
Investment group Umdoni Property Fund added two cents to 182 cents following another bookover involving 5.4 million shares worth around 9.8 million rand, dealers said.

They said black empowerment group New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) also continued to ride high on its Thursday's announcement that it planned to by a stake in the world's third largest gold producer Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd.
Nail finished 55 cents up at 480 cents, making it the JSE's seventh percentage gainer.
On the gold board Vaal Reefs finished down 400 cents at 266.00 rand and Kloof shed 40 cents to end at 30.90 rand.
Dealers said near-dated share futures had been subdued in most of the day's trading with gold contracts also taking a knock on the back of bullion's nervousness.
The June industrial contracts ended at 8,202/10 from the 8,235 settlement, gold contracts at 860/70 from 890 settlement and the all-share at 6,555/65 from 6,605 settlement.
